name: Deiotaros
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Deiotaros was a Continental Celtic god. The Galatae, a Celtic people of Asia Minor, honoured him. His name means "Bull-god" or "divine bull." He may resemble Tarvostrigaranus of Gaul. Tarvostrigaranus carried the same bull power. Both gods anchored their people to strength and the cattle trade.
objective: This entry records the Continental Celtic god Deiotaros, an Earth-bull figure of the Galatae people of Asia Minor.
key_results: Deiotaros was worshipped by the Galatae, a Celtic people living in Asia Minor.
His name translates to "Bull-god" or "divine bull."
He may parallel Tarvostrigaranus of Gaul, another bull-linked deity.
Both figures tied divine power to the bull and the cattle economy.
